about: A hand-built layer on top of the verified rules table in data/rules/. Each entry points back to the field it was taken from (source_field, quoted in source_quote), so a reviewer can check it. Built Oct 17, 2026. The engine reads this file and the verified table, nothing else.

stop_pedaling_class2.decision: These states say the motor must stop when the rider stops pedaling or brakes. Read literally, that clashes with a Class 2 throttle. The verifiers kept Class 2 legal. Class 2 stays legal here too, with one caution line.

fast_mode_rule.about: Every e-bike class caps the motor alone at 20 mph and pedal assist at 28 mph. A bike that can go past either in any mode (throttle, unlock code, app, off-road mode) fits no class. Where verdict_cautions or supplemental_cautions name this, the engine says not an e-bike, and an unanswered question blocks a yes. Everywhere else it says can't confirm, and an unanswered question only adds a caution line.

supplemental_cautions.reason: From Jan 1, 2027, SB 1167 rewrites Cal. Veh. Code 312.5. Its list of vehicles that are not e-bikes includes one that goes over 20 mph on the motor alone, and one whose motor still assists past 28 mph.
supplemental_cautions.citation: Cal. Veh. Code 312.5(c)(2), (3) as rewritten by SB 1167 (Stats. 2026, ch. 846)
supplemental_cautions.source_quote: From Jan 1, 2027 SB 1167 rewrites 312.5 (adds 'e-bike' as a term and lists non-e-bikes: over 750 W, over 20 mph on motor alone, assist past 28 mph
supplemental_cautions.statute_quote: (2) A vehicle capable of attaining a speed greater than 20 miles per hour on motor power alone. (3) A vehicle with a motor capable of providing assistance when the vehicle reaches a speed exceeding 28 miles per hour.
supplemental_cautions.note: Fifth review, Oct 19, 2026: the chaptered text (Sep 30, 2026) was read in a browser on leginfo. SEC. 8 rewrites 312.5, and its subdivision (c) lists vehicles that 'are not electric bicycles under this code'. (c)(2) is a speed over 20 mph on motor power alone, and (c)(3) is assistance past 28 mph. SEC. 8 has no operative date of its own, so it takes effect Jan 1, 2027. (c)(4) also covers a vehicle the manufacturer intends to be modifiable that way, which the fast-mode questions already ask about (unlock codes, app settings, off-road modes). A text mention of an unlock mode alone is not used here, since it could be a legal Class 3 mode.
supplemental_cautions.before_2027: Sixth review, Oct 19, 2026: until Dec 31, 2026 California has no caution here. The 312.5 in force today (SB 1271, effective Jan 1, 2025) was read on leginfo. Its subdivision (d) excludes only a vehicle the manufacturer intends to be modifiable past 20 mph on motor power alone, one modified that way, and one with its pedals removed. A bike that goes past 20 mph on the motor alone as built, with no unlock or modification, still meets 312.5(a) and simply fits no class. So before 2027 a fast mode gets the general fast-mode rule (fits no e-bike class, can't confirm, still NO), not 'not an e-bike' under 312.5(d). The earlier caution with condition motor_only_max_mph > 20 went further than (d) and was removed.

supplemental_cautions.reason: Minn. Stat. 169.011, subd. 27(b)-(c) says a vehicle designed or intended to be configured or modified to exceed its class is not an electric-assisted bicycle.
supplemental_cautions.source_quote: says a vehicle is NOT an e-bike if it is designed or intended to be configured or modified (switch, button, app, motor change) to exceed its class.

supplemental_cautions.reason: Since Jan 1, 2026 an Illinois 'bicycle' needs wheels at least 12 inches across, so a smaller-wheel e-bike may fall outside the definition.
supplemental_cautions.source_quote: Since P.A. 104-141 (eff. Jan 1, 2026), 'bicycle' (§ 1-106) covers low-speed e-bikes 'with 2 or more wheels not less than 12 inches in diameter, operable pedals, and designated seats'.

supplemental_cautions.reason: Louisiana needs one wheel of 16 inches or more on a two-wheeler, or 20 inches or more on a three-wheeler, so a small-wheel e-bike may not qualify.
supplemental_cautions.source_quote: WHEEL SIZE RULE: the bike needs a saddle or seat for each rider and either two tandem wheels, one of which is 16 inches or more in diameter, or three wheels, one of which is 20 inches or more. Small-wheel e-bikes may not qualify.

supplemental_cautions.reason: An Oregon 'bicycle' needs wheels over 14 inches, so a small-wheel e-bike may not qualify.
supplemental_cautions.source_quote: 'Bicycle' (ORS 801.150) needs a seat, no more than 3 wheels, pedals, and every wheel over 14 inches (or two tandem wheels, either over 14 inches). Small-wheel bikes (14 inches or less) therefore may not qualify.

supplemental_cautions.reason: Montana's electrically assisted bicycle has 'two tandem wheels' (MCA 61-8-102), so an electric trike may not be one. Its status was not traced.
supplemental_cautions.source_quote: Three-wheeled e-trikes do not meet the 'two tandem wheels' test and were not traced.

supplemental_cautions.reason: New Jersey's low-speed electric bicycle is 'a two-wheeled vehicle' (N.J.S.A. 39:1-1), and the MVC advisory of June 23, 2026 puts e-trikes outside the law.
supplemental_cautions.source_quote: E-trikes are outside the law per the MVC advisory of June 23, 2026.

supplemental_cautions.reason: Rhode Island's e-bike law covers two wheels only (R.I. Gen. Laws 31-1-3(g)), so an electric trike may not qualify.
supplemental_cautions.source_quote: Two wheels only, and pedals are not expressly required.

age_exceptions.source_quote: Allowed under 16 with 'direct supervision': a supervising parent, guardian or person 18 or older who is physically present and close enough to observe and control the operation (§ 291C-143.5(b)).
Same supervision exception as Class 2. A parent, guardian or person 18 or older must be physically present and in reasonable proximity.
Ages 8 to 13 may ride with the motor engaged only under the direct supervision of a parent or guardian.
Under 14 may ride a Class 3 bike under the immediate supervision of a person 18 or older.

class3_equipment_note: Texas is left out on purpose: its record says the seller or manufacturer must equip a speedometer (Tex. Transp. Code 664.004), which is not a rule for the rider.

class3_equipment.statute_quote: ceases to provide assistance when the bicycle reaches the speed of 28 miles per hour, and equipped with a speedometer.
class3_equipment.note: Read on leginfo on Oct 19, 2026 (as amended by SB 1271, effective Jan 1, 2025) and on FindLaw (current as of Jan 1, 2026). A speedometer is part of the Class 3 definition, so a Class 3 YES lists it as something the bike must have.

road_limits.statute_quote: a bicycle with electric assist may only be operated on highways with a posted speed limit of thirty miles per hour or less
road_limits.note: Fifth review, Oct 19, 2026: read on nysenate.gov. The limit is for e-bikes, not all bicycles, so a New York YES lists it, and the bottom line no longer says the YES covers every public street. 1242(8) also lets a local law or rule allow e-bikes on faster roads.

license_detail.source_quote: Ages 15 and 16 need a motorized bicycle (moped, class F) license or permit. 17 and older need a basic driver's license or a moped license or permit.

watt_fallbacks.source_quote: An electric bike with pedals, a motor up to 1,000 W and a motor-only top speed of no more than 20 mph that does not meet a class (for example 750 W or more) is a 'motor-assisted bicycle'.

Any electric bicycle that is not a low-speed e-bike (so any e-bike at 750 W or more, because the definition stays 'less than 750 watts'), and any electric motor rated greater than 750 W up to 8,000 W, is a motor driven cycle (§§ 1-140.10, 1-145.001).
